newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul media reports former N.Korean premier dead.
newsitem.headline: Seoul media reports former N.Korean premier dead.

text.p: South Korean media reported on Saturday that a former North Korean prime minister had died but Seoul officials declined to confirm the news.

Seoul's state Korea Broadcasting System radio, quoting a diplomatic source, reported former prime minister Kang Song-san, 66, had died on February 22 and that his post was now occupied by former vice premier Kim Dal-hyon.
Kang, ranked sixth in the country's power hierarchy, had long been known to be suffering from diabetes and liver disease.

Pyongyang announced on February 21 that Kang had been replaced by an acting premier, setting off speculation about turmoil in North Korea's leadership since the defection in Beijing early in the month of a top aide to leader Kim Jong-il.
Hwang Jang-yop, the most senior official to defect from the isolated Stalinist state, has been stranded in Seoul's Beijing consulate while China and North and South Korea negotiate his fate.
"We cannot confirm the reports and have no information on Kang's whereabouts," said a spokesman for South Korea's top intelligence body, the Agency for National Security Planning.
"And the Dong-A Ilbo report is not true," he said, referring to a story in the South Korean daily that quoted an unnamed agency official as the source for the report on Kang's death.
South and North Korea are technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce accord, not a peace agreement.

Former vice premier Kim Dal-hyon, Pyongyang's external trading expert, visited Seoul in July 1992 and held meetings with South Korean political and business leaders, including then president Roh Tae-woo.
